generator_metadata.summary: A square 9..11 zero-background grid contains one copy at most of cue colors 1, 2, 3, and 6. Color 6 grows upward into a seven-cell vertical segment, color 3 grows downward into a four-cell vertical segment, color 1 grows a two-cell right arm with a second 1 above its tip, and color 2 is the right endpoint of a five-cell horizontal segment centered on the rightmost non-2 cue to its left. If that horizontal segment crosses the interior of a 6/3 vertical segment, paint a yellow diagonal down-left from the crossing. Ordinary seven-demo lessons cover every canonical cue configuration before querying the same rule on a new placement.

review_brief:
# Review: 4d0f228177b0

Built a complete native two-setting family around a genuine sequential dependency: canonical cue expansion creates a yellow ray; its first adjacent `7/9` payload is the intermediate; that payload color is globally recolored to `8`.

The adversarial pass found and repaired two sampler/lesson shortcuts: remote payloads could hijack the canonical `2`-cue center and suppress the ray, and the two-demo lesson initially leaked the selected color through row-major payload order. It also corrected an over-strong audit assertion that ignored legitimate Step-A overwrites. The retained probe attacks nine semantic rivals, crossed controls, count prefixes, malformed certificates, 30×30/boundary cases, and inactive scenes.

Final authoring evidence passes, including protected-Racket execution, causal ablation, and public-view privacy checks. Limits remain finite: this does not prove universal uniqueness, owner acceptance, or training admission.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: Read the first payload color (7 or 9) adjacent to any yellow ray cell in row-major yellow-cell order after Step A.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Apply the canonical cue expansion: extend 3/6 verticals, expand 1 and 2 cues, and draw the yellow down-left crossing ray when the horizontal crosses a vertical interior.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Recolor every cell of that selected payload color in the Step-A grid to cyan 8, including disconnected remote components.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The input contains no yellow selector ray. Step A creates the yellow cells whose first adjacent payload determines which global color Step B must recolor; skipping Step A leaves the selector absent and changes the final label.
